scope: Named hardy kiwi cultivars: Actinidia arguta (kiwiberry), A. kolomikta and A. polygama (silver vine), including named male pollinators. Fuzzy kiwi (A. deliciosa: Hayward, Saanichton, Elmwood, Jenny and similar) is left out because it isn't reliably hardy in zone 6b. Most hardy kiwis need a male vine nearby; each variety is tagged female, male or self-fertile.

gaps: 'Sentyabraskaya'/'Sientiabrskaja' (kolomikta, Clematis and Marosz 2009) may be the same as 'September Sun' on file; no source links them, so not added.

varieties.name: Anna
varieties.summary: The classic Russian hardy kiwi; sweet, aromatic grape-sized fruit. Needs a male.
varieties.description: Originated in Russia as ‘Ananasnaya’ (“pineapple-like”). One of the most widely grown hardy kiwis in North America, with smooth-skinned, grape-sized green fruit and a sweet, aromatic, tropical flavor; ripens late. Needs a male pollinator nearby.

varieties.name: Issai
varieties.summary: Self-fertile Japanese hardy kiwi: one vine can fruit on its own.
varieties.description: Originated in Japan. The only widely sold hardy kiwi that sets fruit without a male, on a smaller vine that bears in 2–3 years. Grape-sized green fruit with tropical flavor; less cold-hardy than most in University of Minnesota trials, which isn't a concern in zone 6b.

varieties.name: Ken's Red
varieties.summary: Red-skinned hardy kiwi with some of the largest fruit of the type. Needs a male.
varieties.description: A hybrid listed by Logee's as Actinidia purpurea × A. melanandra. Large fruit with red skin and red-blushed flesh and a sweet, rich flavor, eaten skin and all. Needs a male hardy kiwi pollinator.

varieties.name: Dumbarton Oaks
varieties.summary: Early hardy kiwi from Georgetown, DC; ribbed fruit like mini pumpkins.
varieties.description: Selected at Georgetown in Washington, DC. Light green, flattish, ribbed fruit that looks like tiny pumpkins, ripening early (September–October) compared with other hardy kiwis. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Geneva
varieties.summary: Early, sweet hardy kiwi selected in Geneva, New York.
varieties.description: Selected in Geneva, New York. An early-ripening hardy kiwi with sweet green fruit; a common choice for the Northeast. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Geneva 3
varieties.summary: Numbered Geneva selection with tropical-flavored green fruit.
varieties.description: A numbered selection in the Geneva line. Green fruit with tropical flavors; University of Minnesota lists ‘Meader’ as its pollinator.

varieties.name: Michigan State
varieties.summary: Large-fruited hardy kiwi, often sold as MSU.
varieties.description: Sold as ‘Michigan State’ or ‘MSU’; one of the cultivars in Ohio State University's hardy kiwi trials. Large green fruit. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Fortyniner
varieties.summary: Hardy kiwi developed in Chico, California.
varieties.description: Developed in Chico, California. Green, grape-sized fruit; limited independent detail gathered so far. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Cordifolia
varieties.summary: Early-ripening hardy kiwi; part of Ohio State's trials.
varieties.description: Sold as ‘Cordifolia’ or ‘Early Cordifolia’; included in Ohio State University's hardy kiwi trials. Early-ripening green fruit. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Arbor-Eat-Um
varieties.summary: Numbered selection NA-7, sold by Edible Landscaping.
varieties.description: Sold by Edible Landscaping as ‘Arbor-Eat-Um’ (selection NA-7). Limited independent detail gathered so far. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Fifty-Five
varieties.summary: Hardy kiwi sold by Edible Landscaping; limited public detail.
varieties.description: A female hardy kiwi sold by Edible Landscaping. Limited independent detail gathered so far. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Jumbo
varieties.summary: Italian hardy kiwi with large, elongated fruit.
varieties.description: Originated in Italy. Named for its large, elongated fruit, bigger than most hardy kiwis. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Prolific
varieties.summary: Heavy-bearing hardy kiwi; part of Ohio State's trials.
varieties.description: A heavy-bearing hardy kiwi named for its crops; included in Ohio State University's hardy kiwi trials. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Chang Bai
varieties.summary: Large hardy kiwi selected in China near the North Korean border.
varieties.description: A seedling of ‘Qui’ selected in China near the border with North Korea; sold as ‘Chang Bai’ or ‘Chang Bai Giant’ for its large fruit. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Hardy Red
varieties.summary: Red-fleshed hardy kiwi: fruit turns from green to deep red.
varieties.description: A red-fleshed hardy kiwi whose fruit starts green and develops a deep red color as it ripens. Less cold-hardy in University of Minnesota trials, which isn't a concern in zone 6b. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Natasha
varieties.summary: Russian hardy kiwi from Vladivostok; sweet, mango-tropical flavor.
varieties.description: Originated near Vladivostok, Russia. Round green fruit (about 13–16 g) with a sweet, mango-tropical flavor; showed reliable cold hardiness and production in University of Minnesota trials. Needs a male (‘Andrey’ is sold as its partner).

varieties.name: Tatyana
varieties.summary: Russian hardy kiwi; sweet, round green fruit, reliably cold-hardy.
varieties.description: A Russian hardy kiwi with round, sweet green fruit (about 13–16 g) that showed reliable cold hardiness and production in University of Minnesota trials. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Rossana
varieties.summary: Italian hardy kiwi selection.
varieties.description: Selected in Italy. Limited independent detail gathered so far. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Silver Lining
varieties.summary: Variegated hardy kiwi grown for its foliage as well as fruit.
varieties.description: A female hardy kiwi with variegated leaves, sold by One Green World as much for its ornamental foliage as its fruit. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Meader Female
varieties.summary: Female counterpart sold under the Meader name by One Green World.
varieties.description: A female hardy kiwi sold by One Green World as ‘Meader Female’, separate from the well-known ‘Meader’ male pollinator. Limited independent detail. Needs a male.

varieties.summary: Numbered female selection sold by Tripple Brook Farm.
varieties.description: A numbered female selection sold by Tripple Brook Farm. Limited independent detail gathered so far. Needs a male.

varieties.name: September Sun
varieties.summary: Russian kolomikta; small, very cold-hardy vine.
varieties.description: An Actinidia kolomikta that originated in Russia. Kolomikta is the hardiest kiwi, with smaller (3–7 g) fruit and more floral, kiwi-like flavor than arguta. Needs a kolomikta male.

varieties.name: Krupnoplodnaya
varieties.summary: Large-fruited kolomikta; reliably cold-hardy in Minnesota trials.
varieties.description: An Actinidia kolomikta whose name means “large-fruited”; it bears on the larger side for the species (3–7 g) and was reliably cold-hardy in University of Minnesota trials. Needs a kolomikta male.

varieties.name: Red Beauty
varieties.summary: Kolomikta sold by Tripple Brook Farm; limited public detail.
varieties.description: An Actinidia kolomikta sold by Tripple Brook Farm. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Emerald
varieties.summary: Female Arctic Beauty kolomikta sold by Raintree.
varieties.description: Sold by Raintree as Emerald™ Arctic Beauty, a female Actinidia kolomikta. Needs a kolomikta male such as Pasha™.

varieties.name: Arctic Beauty
varieties.summary: Ornamental male kolomikta with pink, white and green leaves.
varieties.description: A male Actinidia kolomikta grown for striking pink, white and green variegated leaves; pollinates kolomikta females but bears no fruit itself. Patented (USPP 8624).

varieties.name: Pasha
varieties.summary: Male Arctic Beauty kolomikta pollinator.
varieties.description: Sold as Pasha™ Arctic Beauty, a male Actinidia kolomikta that pollinates kolomikta females.

varieties.name: Vera's Pride
varieties.summary: Female silver vine (A. polygama) sold by Raintree.
varieties.description: A female Actinidia polygama (silver vine) sold by Raintree. Silver vine bears small, tart-to-sweet fruit and is famously attractive to cats. Needs a polygama male such as Pavel™.

varieties.name: Hot Pepper
varieties.summary: Female silver vine (A. polygama) sold by Raintree.
varieties.description: A female Actinidia polygama (silver vine) sold by Raintree. Needs a polygama male.

varieties.name: Pavel
varieties.summary: Male silver vine pollinator.
varieties.description: A male Actinidia polygama (silver vine) sold by Raintree to pollinate silver vine females.

varieties.name: Meader
varieties.summary: Widely used male pollinator for hardy kiwi.
varieties.description: A named male Actinidia arguta widely sold as a pollinator; University of Minnesota lists it for ‘Geneva 3’ and other females. Bears no fruit.

varieties.name: Clark
varieties.summary: Male pollinator (selection 74-46) for hardy kiwi.
varieties.description: A male Actinidia arguta sold as ‘Clark’, also known as selection 74-46; Logee's pairs it with ‘Anna’ and ‘Ken's Red’. Bears no fruit.

varieties.summary: Numbered male pollinator selection.
varieties.description: A numbered male Actinidia arguta selection sold as a pollinator. Bears no fruit.

varieties.name: Fairchild
varieties.summary: Male pollinator (selection 74-52).
varieties.description: A male Actinidia arguta sold as ‘Fairchild’, also known as selection 74-52. Bears no fruit.

varieties.name: Opitz
varieties.summary: Male pollinator sold by Tripple Brook Farm.
varieties.description: A male Actinidia arguta sold as a pollinator by Tripple Brook Farm. Bears no fruit.

varieties.name: Flowercloud
varieties.summary: Male pollinator sold by One Green World.
varieties.description: A male Actinidia arguta sold by One Green World as a pollinator. Bears no fruit.

varieties.name: Ogden Point
varieties.summary: Female hardy kiwi sold by Spring Hill Nurseries, paired with a male pollinator.
varieties.description: A female Actinidia arguta sold by Spring Hill Nurseries as part of a female+male pair. Limited independent detail gathered so far. Needs a male.

varieties.name: Andrey
varieties.summary: Russian male hardy kiwi pollinator, paired with Natasha and Tatyana.
varieties.description: A male Actinidia arguta discovered near Vladivostok, Russia alongside the female cultivars 'Natasha' and 'Tatyana', which it is especially suited to pollinate. Bears no fruit; one male can pollinate up to eight females.

varieties.name: Red Princess
varieties.summary: Red-and-green-fleshed hardy kiwi sold by One Green World.
varieties.description: A female Actinidia arguta with bright red-and-green flesh and a sweet-tart, grape-like flavor eaten skin and all. Vigorous vine hardy to -25F (USDA zones 4-9); begins bearing 3-4 years after planting, ripening September-October. Needs a male pollinator.

varieties.name: Cherry Bomb
varieties.summary: Red-fruited hardy kiwi, possibly a kolomikta cross. Needs a male.
varieties.description: A female Actinidia arguta sold as 'Cherry Bomb' (or 'Cherrybomb'); some sellers describe it as possibly a cross with A. kolomikta. Sweet, red-skinned fruit on a vine with large, lush foliage. Needs a male hardy kiwi.

varieties.name: Chico State
varieties.summary: Prolific green-fruited hardy kiwi that ripens about a week before Anna.
varieties.description: A female Actinidia arguta sold as 'Chico State' (or 'Chico'). Described by sellers as a prolific producer of large, sweet green fruit that separates easily from the stem, ripening about a week before 'Anna'. Needs a male.

varieties.name: USDA Male
varieties.summary: New Hampshire male kolomikta selection that pollinates Arctic Beauty females.
varieties.description: A male Actinidia kolomikta selected in New Hampshire, with somewhat less leaf variegation than Pasha. It flowers heavily and one male can pollinate up to 8 kolomikta females. Bears no fruit; hardy to about -40F (zones 3-7).

varieties.name: Dr. Szymanowski
varieties.summary: Polish kolomikta with variegated leaves, sold as self-fertile.
varieties.description: A Polish Actinidia kolomikta selection named after a horticulturist, with leaves splashed pink and white on mature plants. Small (about 2 cm) sweet green-yellow fruit ripens in late summer to early fall; nurseries sell it as self-fertile, though a Polish study reported it acted as a female, so a kolomikta male may still help. Very cold-hardy: it was among the least winter-damaged cultivars in a central-Poland hardiness trial, but slow-growing.
varieties.one_liner: The very cold-hardy kolomikta sold as self-fertile
notes: Self-fertility is disputed: sellers and a Russian botanic-garden paper call it self-fertile/hermaphroditic, but a Polish study quoted on Growing Fruit found it female-acting.

varieties.name: Adam
varieties.summary: Polish male kolomikta grown as a pollinator and for its pink-and-white leaves.
varieties.description: A male Actinidia kolomikta selected by Szczepan Marczyński in Poland and introduced in 2001. It bears no fruit but flowers with white, slightly scented blooms in early summer and pollinates all kolomikta females; older plants show creamy-white leaf variegation that flushes pink in summer.
varieties.one_liner: The variegated male that pollinates any kolomikta

varieties.name: Vitakola
varieties.summary: Czech kolomikta with unusually large fruit for the species.
varieties.description: A Czech Actinidia kolomikta cultivar noted for fruit that is exceptionally large for the species, tasty and borne in heavy crops. It also has ornamental variegated leaves and lemon-scented flowers. Needs a kolomikta male.
varieties.one_liner: The kolomikta with unusually big fruit for the species

varieties.name: Bailey's
varieties.summary: Self-fertile kolomikta (Arctic Beauty) sold by One Green World.
varieties.description: An Actinidia kolomikta sold by One Green World as Bailey's Arctic Beauty, described as self-fertile, though yields are said to improve with a Pasha male nearby. Sweet green fruit eaten skin and all ripens in August, and the leaves are variegated green, white and pink. Very cold-hardy, to about -40F (zones 3-7).
varieties.one_liner: The self-fertile Arctic Beauty, for a one-vine kolomikta
notes: A Growing Fruit forum member suspects it may be a renamed Dr. Szymanowski; unconfirmed.

varieties.name: Weiki
varieties.summary: German hardy kiwi with medium green fruit that hangs on the vine.
varieties.description: A German Actinidia arguta grown in both female and male forms; the female is very productive. Medium green fruit (about 2.5-3 cm) takes a dark brown blush in sun, ripens late (October) and does not drop. Hardy to about -30C (-22F), with red leaf stalks. Needs a male such as Weiki Male.
varieties.one_liner: The late, heavy-bearing hardy kiwi whose fruit doesn't drop

varieties.name: Weiki Male
varieties.summary: German male hardy kiwi used to pollinate arguta females.
varieties.description: The male form of the German Actinidia arguta 'Weiki', grown to pollinate arguta females; it bears no fruit. Creamy-white, slightly scented flowers appear in early summer on a vine with red twining stems. RHS rates it hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe.
varieties.one_liner: The male that pollinates any arguta female

varieties.name: Bingo
varieties.summary: Polish hardy kiwi with pineapple-flavored fruit.
varieties.description: A Polish Actinidia arguta (protected by plant breeders' rights) bearing plentiful, sweet, aromatic fruit with a pineapple flavor. A European seller describes the roughly 3 cm fruit as dark pink with yellow flesh, ripening September to October, on a very hardy vine. Not self-fertile; needs a male.

varieties.name: Purpurna Sadowa
varieties.summary: Ukrainian purple kiwi, red in full sun.
varieties.description: A Ukrainian female, probably from Actinidia purpurea seedlings or an arguta x purpurea cross (RHS lists it under A. arguta var. purpurea). Oval fruit about 3.5 cm long turns purple-red in full sun and stays green in shade; it keeps well and ripens mid-September to mid-October. Hardy to about -25C (-13F). Needs a male.
varieties.one_liner: The purple-red one that keeps well

varieties.name: Rogow
varieties.summary: Polish hardy kiwi selected at the Rogów Arboretum.
varieties.description: A Polish Actinidia arguta female selected at the Arboretum in Rogów. Very productive, with green fruit about 2.5-3 cm long that ripens late September to early October. Hardy to about -30C (-22F). Needs a male.
varieties.one_liner: The productive Polish one from Rogów

varieties.name: Scarlet September
varieties.summary: Polish red hardy kiwi, the earliest to ripen.
varieties.description: A Polish Actinidia arguta sold under the trade name Scarlet September Kiwi, with sweet red fruit. Its nursery calls it the earliest of all its cultivars to ripen, from late August to mid-September. Pollination needs are not stated by the source; most arguta need a male.
varieties.one_liner: The early red one that starts the season in August

varieties.name: Vitikiwi
varieties.summary: Hardy kiwi that sets usually seedless fruit without pollination.
varieties.description: An Actinidia arguta sold under the trade name Vitikiwi that is parthenocarpic, setting fruit without pollination, so it needs no male. Productive from its first or second year, with green, usually seedless fruit (few seeds) ripening in October.
varieties.one_liner: The one that fruits with no male and few seeds

varieties.name: Hortgem Tahi
varieties.summary: New Zealand kiwiberry bred for sweet, early, long-storing fruit.
varieties.description: Bred in New Zealand by HortResearch from a 1987 cross and selected in 1998. Small green, hairless fruit averages about 11 g with high sugar (about 20 Brix) and a sweet, aromatic flavor; it is early-ripening (about three months from flowering) and stores 10-12 weeks chilled. Strong vine that bears from year two. Needs a male.
varieties.one_liner: The very sweet commercial kiwiberry that stores for weeks

breeder.name: Horticulture and Food Research Institute of New Zealand (HortResearch, now Plant & Food Research)

varieties.name: Hortgem Rua
varieties.summary: New Zealand kiwiberry with red-centered flesh.
varieties.description: Bred in New Zealand by HortResearch from a cross made in 1987 and selected in 1998. Oblong fruit averages about 16 g, with skin that blushes red-purple and a red center at maturity; the flesh is tender and sweet-aromatic, with a shorter storage life (3-5 weeks chilled). Medium-vigor vine that bears from year two. Needs a male.
varieties.one_liner: The red-centered kiwiberry from New Zealand

breeder.name: Horticulture and Food Research Institute of New Zealand (HortResearch, now Plant & Food Research)

varieties.name: Hortgem Wha
varieties.summary: New Zealand kiwiberry, a sister to Hortgem Tahi.
varieties.description: Bred in New Zealand by HortResearch from a cross with Japanese seed-family parentage, selected in 1998. Small oblong green fruit (about 8-10 g) is sweet and aromatic (about 17 Brix), early-ripening, and stores 6-8 weeks chilled. Strong vine that bears from year two. Needs a male.
varieties.one_liner: The small, sweet, early kiwiberry from New Zealand

breeder.name: Horticulture and Food Research Institute of New Zealand (HortResearch, now Plant & Food Research)
